skill.name: codebase-analysis
skill.description: Analyze a project codebase to map structure, dependencies, architecture, quality signals, and practical next steps.
skill.summary: Create structured codebase analysis reports for project onboarding, planning, and technical review.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, fenced examples, and file-name references. The real risks are the skill's recommendation to run project-controlled NPM scripts and package-manager commands, especially because the skill is configured for auto-invocation.

remediation.issue: Auto-invoked Bash execution of project scripts
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npm, pnpm, or any package script, and explain that project scripts can execute arbitrary code.

remediation.issue: Package-manager audit and outdated commands may make network requests
remediation.suggestion: Document that dependency audit commands can contact registries, and offer a static lock-file review when network access is not approved.
Clarify that .env files should be detected by name only unless the user explicitly approves reading local secret-bearing files.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Identify project type** by reading `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or framework-specific confi
- Next.js: Check for `next` in dependencies, `next.config.*`, `app/` or `pages/` directory
- Run linter if available: `npm run lint` (via Bash)
- Find test files: Use Glob for `**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}`
- Calculate coverage: Run `npm run test:coverage` if available
- `quality-gates` - Use analysis results to run appropriate quality checks
- `project-initialization` - Compare against templates to identify missing setup
- Framework-specific skills (`nextjs-optimization`, `react-patterns`) - Auto-invoke based on detecte

content.value_statement: New or unfamiliar repositories can hide important structure, dependency, and quality risks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured codebase analysis report.
actual_capabilities: Maps source, test, config, documentation, and build-output directories.
Identifies common frontend frameworks from package metadata and file patterns.
Reviews package dependencies, scripts, engine requirements, and lock files.
Searches for architecture patterns, API routes, state management, and authentication markers.
Checks quality signals such as linting setup, tests, TypeScript strictness, TODOs, and console logs.
Produces a structured Markdown report with recommendations, risk areas, and next steps.
limitations: It depends on available repository files and may miss generated or external architecture details.
Running lint, coverage, audit, or outdated commands needs user approval in untrusted projects.
Large repositories may require targeted analysis by directory or feature area.
It reports indicators and recommendations, not a formal security certification.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a New Repository
use_cases.description: Build a concise map of structure, stack, dependencies, and important workflows before making changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Identify architecture patterns, code-quality signals, and technical debt areas that should shape a refactor plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Project Review
use_cases.description: Create a structured report covering stack, tests, risks, recommendations, and next steps for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Repository Overview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a high-level orientation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository at a high level. Summarize the project type, main directories, core dependencies, and the first risks I should understand.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture and Patterns Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on structure and conventions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the codebase architecture. Identify file organization, framework patterns, API boundaries, state management, and conventions that future changes should follow.

prompt_templates.title: Quality and Dependency Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review code quality and dependencies. Check linting, formatting, tests, TypeScript strictness, package scripts, lock files, and visible technical debt indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Targeted Modernization Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for planning larger engineering work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository for modernization planning. Prioritize architecture risks, dependency risks, quality gaps, and practical sequencing for the next three engineering improvements.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Next.js repository before I add a new dashboard feature.
output_examples.output: A report summarizing the Next.js structure, app or pages routing, UI libraries, state patterns, test setup, quality signals, and dashboard-specific risks.

output_examples.input: Review this project for technical debt before a refactor.
output: Architecture overview with directory and module patterns.
Quality metrics covering TypeScript, linting, tests, TODOs, and console logs.
Prioritized recommendations and risk areas for the refactor plan.

output_examples.input: Give me a dependency and security overview without running commands yet.
output_examples.output: A static review of package metadata, lock-file presence, scripts, dependency categories, and recommended commands that need approval before execution.

best_practices: Start with static file inspection before approving any Bash or package-manager command.
Ask for targeted analysis when the repository is very large or the task concerns one feature area.
Use the recommendations section to create concrete follow-up tasks with owners and priorities.
anti_patterns: Do not run package scripts from an untrusted repository without explicit user approval.
Do not treat the generated report as complete security assurance for production release.
Do not read local secret files unless the user has clearly approved that scope.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes repository structure, technology stack, dependencies, architecture patterns, quality signals, risks, and next steps.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill mentions Bash commands, but users should approve package-manager commands before execution in untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Can it analyze frontend projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, routing, UI libraries, and styling tools.

faq.question: Can it find security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can guide dependency audit checks and risk review, but it is not a full security scanner.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a Markdown report with project overview, technology stack, architecture, quality metrics, recommendations, risks, and next steps.
